8kk0pa.title: 1 BTC is hidden in this puzzle. Good luck!

evidence.summary: The OP describes a work made from Satoshi whitepaper words with a treasure hunt hidden in plain sight; clues explicitly act on visible words.
One published clue tells solvers that at least half of the visible words can be discarded.
The OP repeatedly publishes the clue 'Think in pairs'.
Public solve work uses start points, segmented regions, directions and ordered paths through visible words; the OP's positional clues support an ordered spatial reading.
No made-up character alphabet comparable to 8krbd3 is established in the public thread.
Numbers appear in clues, but no custom numeral alphabet is established as a confirmed mechanism.
The image is explicitly constructed from Satoshi Nakamoto's whitepaper words and multiple clues/solver observations use that known source text.
Published clues include a marked start/home concept and spatial instructions; solver work explicitly tests positions, regions, angles and paths.
Visible linguistic/spatial information is transformed through several interpretive steps into wallet-unlocking material.
The OP reduced one major step for difficulty, but a final brute-force step is not established in the public evidence used here.
The public mechanism discussion centers on visible words, positions and clues rather than exact pixel values.
The puzzle visibly presents a made-up character set that solvers translate as letters/phonetic sounds and number symbols.
No separate discard/filter stage comparable to 8kk0pa is established.
Upper/lowercase sharing a keyboard key is discussed, but no general pair-selection step is established.
The visible custom symbols are read in their displayed order to reconstruct the encoded wallet-key text.
The OP explicitly calls it a made-up character set and explains a typo involving symbols bound to upper/lowercase on the same key.
Solvers separately infer number symbols using arithmetic examples; the OP confirms the symbols represent whole numbers.
No external canonical text is required as a confirmed decoding source.
The confirmed work is symbol translation rather than coordinate or geometric extraction.
Visible invented glyphs are converted through phonetic/letter and numeral interpretations into wallet-key text.
A solver reports brute-forcing remaining allowed case switches after most symbols were decoded.
The mechanism is based on human-readable drawn glyphs; exact source-pixel values are not established as required.

transfer_rule: Only operations marked confirmed in both independent top pre-launch candidates may be promoted as a mechanism-family prior. Candidate-specific operations remain non-transferable.
